# DH-ADOM v1.0
## DevHeal Hierarchical Agent Development & Orchestration Model

DH-ADOM is a repository-level operating model for governed AI-native software engineering.

### Package map

- `01-White-Paper/` — public technical narrative.
- `02-Specification/` — normative model, schemas, state machines, API definitions, conformance requirements.
- `03-Reference-Templates/` — normative repository and agent templates.
- `04-Reference-Implementation/` — small executable reference implementation of the core semantics.
- `05-Conformance-Validation-Suite/` — implementation-neutral validation requirements and runnable checks.
- `06-Benchmarks-Experiments/` — reproducible benchmark task definitions and analysis tooling. No performance claims are included without measured data.
- `07-Architecture-Diagrams/` — editable source, SVG, PNG, Mermaid, and publication assets.
- `08-Research-Publications/` — prior-art review, standards mapping, bibliography, and publication notes.
- `09-Version-History/` — changelog, release notes, and roadmap.
- `10-Website/` — website-ready content, metadata, citation blocks, and publication page.
- `11-Licensing-and-Citation/` — licensing, citation, and archival metadata.

### Core hierarchy

```text
Engineering Constitution
        ↓
AI-SDLC
        ↓
ADLC
        ↓
Root / Main Orchestrator Agent
        ↓
Feature / Domain Agents
        ↓
Bounded Specialist Agents
        ↓
Implementation + Validation
        ↓
Evidence + Handoff
        ↓
Root Review + Integration
        ↓
Continuous AI-SDLC Feedback
```

### Publication status

Version: `1.0.0`
Release date: `2026-10-06`
Status: `Public Technical Release`

This package is a technical model and reference implementation. It does not claim that hierarchical agents, orchestrator-worker patterns, AI-SDLC, ADLC, agent identity, or agent security controls were invented by DevHeal Labs AI. The proposed contribution is their specific composition into a repository-native operating model centered on persistent feature ownership, bounded delegation, lifecycle governance, evidence, and AI-resumable development.
